summary: Durfee Hill lookout, a 65-ft steel tower first operated in 1926; moved to Buck Hill in 1937, where NHLR lists a standing tower. Durfee Hill site: no tower described.

facts.status_note: Tower moved to Buck Hill in Burrillville in 1937. The Durfee Hill site is a former lookout site and no source describes a tower or remains there now. The Buck Hill tower is listed as standing.
facts.agency: Rhode Island Commissioner of Forestry, later the Department of Agriculture and Conservation

access.note: The tower now stands on Buck Hill. The register's 2017 visit report there says 'No public access'. No source gives access for the Durfee Hill site.

events.note: January 1916 forestry commissioner's report proposes a lookout on Durfee Hill and mentions buying the Durfee Hill region as a state forest reserve
Register says the tower was first operated in 1926
Ended operation at the end of the 1937 fire season
1937 annual report, as quoted: only four existing towers of real value; a tower on Buck Hill in Burrillville would complete coverage; the Blackstone Valley tower has been moved to Buck Hill
Register gives 1938 as the build year of the Buck Hill tower; it is not stated whether this is the erection date of the moved tower (see resolved_conflicts)
Registered September 8, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg

corrections.why: The tower was moved to Buck Hill in 1937 according to the 1937 annual report as quoted on the source page. The Durfee Hill site itself has no tower.

corrections.proposed: Rhode Island Commissioner of Forestry, later the Department of Agriculture and Conservation
corrections.why: (WOONSOCKET) is the town label printed on the source page, not an agency. The source quotes the Forestry Commissioner's January 1916 report and the Department of Agriculture and Conservation's 1937 annual report.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list has a Blackstone entry at 41.91909, -71.48684, about 21 km east of the register's Durfee Hill point at 41.89175, -71.7437. The list does not say whether it is the same site, so the record keeps the register's coordinates.

The register gives 1938 for the Buck Hill tower, while the 1937 annual report, as quoted, says the Blackstone Valley tower had already been moved there. Neither source explains the one-year gap, so the 1938 date is not treated as the move date.

notes_for_editor: The move to Buck Hill rests on one quoted 1937 annual report on the Forest Lookouts site; the Buck Hill record (us-ri-buck-hill) is consistent with it and treats the 1938 date as an inference. Durfee Hill site access and today's remains are undescribed by any source. The WWII radio claim comes only from the NHLR page and is uncorroborated. The brief's agency '(WOONSOCKET)' is a town label, and the brief's status 'gone' is right for the Durfee site but understates the move. Coordinate conflict with the FFLA Blackstone entry is unresolved.
